title: Characterisation of certificate stripping
statement: For every binary string $v$, stripping $v$ is undefined if and only if $v$ consists entirely of zeros. For every binary string $u$, stripping $v$ returns $u$ if and only if $v$ is $u$ followed by a $1$ and then some finite number of zeros.
hypotheses_covered: The first equivalence characterises when stripping $v$ is undefined
For every binary string $u$, the second equivalence characterises when stripping $v$ returns $u
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{strip}$ be the partial map on binary strings defined by:
$\mathrm{strip}(\varepsilon)$ is undefined, and for a bit $b$ and a string $v$,
$\mathrm{strip}(bv) = b\,\mathrm{strip}(v)$ when $\mathrm{strip}(v)$ is defined,
while otherwise $\mathrm{strip}(1v) = \varepsilon$ and $\mathrm{strip}(0v)$ is
undefined. Then for every binary string $v$: $\mathrm{strip}(v)$ is undefined if
and only if $v = 0^{|v|}$ consists only of zeros; and for every binary string $u$,
$\mathrm{strip}(v) = u$ if and only if $v = u\,1\,0^k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
